content.text:
I found and addressed a deviation. Summary:

**The planner hint was wrong.** It predicted no liquidated damages were visible (`likelyAbsent: true`, pointing only at the title paragraph). A search for "liquidated damages" returned nothing, but searching "terminat" surfaced Section 4.2 — a Customer-payable stipulated sum that simply isn't labelled as liquidated damages.

**The problem (p0026).** In any Company termination, Deerskin pays HDI 50% of trailing twelve-month Net Sales above $800,000. Cross-checking the fee clause (§3.1: 30% of Net Sales above $11,000/month) shows this exceeds a full year of actual fees — at $2m Net Sales, ~$560k/yr in fees versus a ~$600k termination payment. That clears the walk-away threshold of "exceeding the remaining contract value."

Three aggravating features:
- Triggered by *any* Company termination, including ordinary non-renewal on 90 days' notice under §4.1 and termination for HDI's own breach (only the narrow §1.6 late-launch right is "without penalty").
- Fully one-way: §4.1 lets HDI walk on identical notice for free, and p0028 confirms HDI never pays us.
- Direction is correctly ours — the Company is our client, so this is a Customer-payable amount, not a compliant vendor-side credit.

**Why fallback rather than deletion.** §1.2 puts all Site design, development, hosting and promotion costs on HDI, recouped only through the revenue share. Some early-termination compensation is therefore part of the real bargain, making outright deletion disproportionate — and the playbook's redline guidance expressly contemplates capping an unavoidable fee at 3 months' fees. The redline caps the payment at three months' §3.1 fees, makes it the sole monetary remedy, and disapplies it where we terminate for HDI's breach or under §1.6.

One drafting note for your review: I left §4.2(b) (p0027–p0028) untouched to keep the edit minimal. Its "less than or equal to zero" mechanic still functions under the new formula but is now largely vestigial, so you may want to tidy it if the cap is accepted.
